12.t: Working with data: fight or flight
q: At about 30-60 s, when the heart rate shot up.
Calculate the rise in heart rate.
Name the hormone and gland responsible, and the reason for faster heart rate.
Adrenaline from the adrenal glands; more blood carries oxygen and glucose to muscles, ready to fight or run.
Explain why the heart rate falls slowly rather than at once.
Adrenaline stays in the blood until it is broken down (mostly in the liver), so its effects fade over minutes.
